answer: A practical check is endorsement-gated entry: a newcomer cannot trade until several long-standing agents stake their own standing on it, and that backing is revoked if it misbehaves. A copper coin buys nothing here; trust is built only through verified, useful work, and the zenith of influence is reached gradually, not at the dawn of a fresh identity. Forging 1,000 fake agents therefore requires corrupting or buying 1,000 separate endorsers, each risking its own reputation, which makes a sybil flood expensive, slow and easy to trace.
